Rob Gronkowski: Played college football at the University of Arizona.
Caught 17 touchdown passes in 2011, a single-season record for a tight end.
Won four Super Bowls: three with New England and one with Tampa Bay.
Wore number 87 and was famous for his ball-spiking celebrations.
Tony Gonzalez: Played both football and basketball at Cal.
Was selected 13th overall by Kansas City in the 1997 NFL draft.
Spent 12 seasons with Kansas City before finishing his career in Atlanta.
Retired in 2013 with more catches than any tight end in NFL history.
Travis Kelce: Played college football at the University of Cincinnati.
Won three Super Bowls with Kansas City.
His older brother was a longtime center for the Philadelphia Eagles.
Co-hosts the New Heights podcast with his brother.

Anthony Muñoz: Was selected third overall by Cincinnati in the 1980 NFL draft.
A left tackle who was picked for 11 Pro Bowls.
Played in two Super Bowls, losing both to San Francisco.
Larry Allen: Played college football at Sonoma State, a Division II school.
Was drafted by Dallas in the second round in 1994.
Won a Super Bowl ring with Dallas after the 1995 season.
Remembered as one of the strongest men ever to play the game.
Jonathan Ogden: Played college football at UCLA, where he also threw the shot put.
Was the first draft pick in Baltimore Ravens history, in 1996.
Won a Super Bowl with Baltimore after the 2000 season.
A 6-foot-9 left tackle who spent his whole career with one team.

Reggie White: Played college football at the University of Tennessee.
Starred for Philadelphia before a landmark free-agent move.
Won a Super Bowl with Green Bay after the 1996 season.
Aaron Donald: Played college football at the University of Pittsburgh.
Spent his whole career with the Rams, in St. Louis and Los Angeles.
Won NFL Defensive Player of the Year three times.
His late pressure on fourth down sealed the Super Bowl LVI win.
J.J. Watt: Walked on at Wisconsin after starting his college career at Central Michigan.
Was selected 11th overall by Houston in the 2011 NFL draft.
Had two seasons with 20 or more sacks.
Raised tens of millions of dollars for Hurricane Harvey relief.

Lawrence Taylor: Played college football at North Carolina.
Was selected second overall in the 1981 NFL draft.
Won two Super Bowls with the New York Giants.
Was named NFL MVP in 1986, a rare honor for a defender.
Ray Lewis: Played college football at the University of Miami.
Spent all 17 of his seasons with the Baltimore Ravens.
Was named MVP of Super Bowl XXXV.
Won a second Super Bowl in his final season.
Dick Butkus: Played college football at the University of Illinois.
A Chicago native who spent his whole career with the hometown Bears.
College football's award for the top linebacker is named after him.

Deion Sanders: Played college football at Florida State.
Won Super Bowls with San Francisco and Dallas.
Also played Major League Baseball during his NFL career.
Ed Reed: Played college football at the University of Miami.
A ballhawking safety who spent most of his career in Baltimore.
Was named NFL Defensive Player of the Year in 2004.
Won a Super Bowl with Baltimore after the 2012 season.
Ronnie Lott: Won four Super Bowls with San Francisco.
Started at cornerback, then moved to safety.
Had the tip of a finger amputated rather than miss playing time.
